title: finding(skills): objectstack-ai's Common Pitfalls says "`memory` is declared only — no runtime reads it"; once PR #21413 lands, the cloud AI runtime enforces it and the spec refuses its old shapes
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect, class (c)**, a teaching error in published text an AI author reads. `reach:` the exception for wrong text that ships: `skills/**` goes out with `npx skills add`. `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` priority rule 4: 「写给 AI 的文档与 skills 说错一句,等于产品缺陷」. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (`session_01YDt3PzwfrkuFzUBF89WPmM`, seat post #18549), from the #20274 `agent.memory` dev report `5953769101` (out-of-scope finding 1). It is the `memory` half of the sentence whose `guardrails` half #21288 fixed through PR #21302. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

**Who acts on it:** the `skills/**` lane. It is a Tier H surface and lands by human approval in its own PR. It should ship in the same release as PR #21413. Neither publishes on merge: the release is the Version Packages PR.

**Dedupe:** the ~1,000 most recently updated issues and PRs here, open and closed, were listed by REST and grepped for `declared only` or `objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` together with `memory`. That gave 4 hits:
- PR #21280 (closed; the `guardrails` flip);
- #21288 (closed `completed`; the `guardrails` / `outputSchema` text);
- PR #21302 (closed; that text's fix, which kept the `memory` clause because `memory` was then unenforced);
- PR #21413 (open; the source of this finding).

None carries the `memory` clause after the change.

## The position (read at `main`)

`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:311-313`, Common Pitfalls 1: "… but it is a limit, not an approval; `memory` is declared only — no runtime reads it."

## What PR #21413 makes true (ruling A′ `5950198150` on #20274)

- **`agent.memory` is enforced by the cloud AI runtime.** The `agent.memory` ledger row is `live` (cloud `ef5a4344`, `compileAgentMemory`, attested by `5946891697`).
- **When `longTerm.enabled` is true,** `maxEntries` and `reflectionInterval` are required. `reflectionInterval` without an enabled `longTerm` is refused.
- **`longTerm.store` is retired:** storage is the platform's.

## The fix

Rewrite the clause to say that `memory` is enforced by the AI runtime ☁️: long-term notes are recalled and reflected on, with `maxEntries` and `reflectionInterval` required when `longTerm.enabled`, and no storage backend to choose. Keep the sentence's point that none of these is a gate. Nothing else in the pitfall changes.
